claims.exact_statement: For every explicitly represented finite simple undirected unweighted graph G and rational 0<eps<1, 0<delta<1/2, the pinned manuscript claims a classical FPRAS for the number Z(G) of perfect matchings, returning zero with certainty if Z(G)=0, otherwise a relative-eps estimate with failure at most delta, in worst-case bit time polynomial in the full input length, eps^-1, and log(delta^-1).
claims.status: source-reported; main theorem not independently proof-validated in this subtask
claims.novelty_boundary: The release theorem is the substantive candidate claim; source-reported and externally unreviewed here.
claims.costs: Worst-case polynomial bit time in input length, eps^-1, log(delta^-1) as stated by the source. Its internal rational activities are charged in source Section 9; arbitrary input edge weights are not covered.
claims.falsifier: A counterexample to a load-bearing proof lemma or an implementation/bit bound violation in the pinned theorem proof.
claims.next_gate: Independent expert proof review or source artifact/formal replay of the full counting algorithm.

claims.exact_statement: Conditional on QFCS-1, every simple graph with a perfect matching admits a uniform classical randomized sampler that outputs a perfect matching on every execution and whose output law is within TV tau of uniform, in worst-case bit time polynomial in input length and tau^-1; infeasibility is detected exactly.
assumptions: QFCS-1 count FPRAS is valid on every residual simple graph
Fresh randomness for each adaptive count call
claims.status: internally reconstructed conditional theorem; algebraic TV audit completed
claims.novelty_boundary: Not a new sampling principle: Jerrum-Valiant-Vazirani (1986) give the self-reducible count/sample equivalence, and the pinned manuscript already states Lemma 10.2. The claim is TV approximation, not exact or pointwise-uniform sampling.
claims.costs: With m0 edges and m*=max(1,m0), set eta=gamma=tau/(8m*) and t=ceil(log2(8m*/tau)); at most 2m0 FPRAS calls, each (eta,gamma), at most 2m0+1 exact feasibility tests, at most m0 branch decisions, exactly t fair bits per non-forced decision, and exact rational ratio/floor arithmetic. Conditional branch error beta=eta/[2(1-eta)]+2gamma+2^-t<=4eta; total TV<=m0 beta<=tau/2<tau. Worst-case polynomial bit time follows from QFCS-1.
claims.falsifier: A feasible history with branch-law TV greater than beta, an infeasible branch selected, failure of the exact-ratio path telescoping, or an execution exceeding the stated oracle-call/random-bit bounds.
claims.next_gate: Keep as a checked corollary; pursue a different target if the root needs novelty beyond the release theorem.

claims.exact_statement: Conditional on QFCS-1, fixed-cardinality matchings and prescribed-degree edge subsets in explicitly listed simple unweighted graphs inherit relative-error counting FPRASs with certain-zero detection and TV-tau feasible samplers via the constant-fibre gadgets in source Section 10.
assumptions: Binary encoded k or vertex demands
No edge weights or compressed multiplicities
Objects are labeled edge subsets, not isomorphism classes
claims.novelty_boundary: Already included in the pinned manuscript as Corollary 10.1; a direct consequence, not a new result here.
claims.costs: For k-matchings use q=n-2k labeled dummies; gadget size <=2n vertices and m+n^2 edges; each k-matching has q! lifts, with log(q!)=O(n log(n+1)). For f-factors, use one incidence port and dv-fv labeled dummies per vertex; gadget has <=4m vertices and <=m+2m(n-1) edges; constant fibre product_v(dv-fv)! has O(m log(n+1)) bits. Count estimates divide by the fibre using exact rational arithmetic; deterministic projection preserves the TV upper bound.
claims.falsifier: Any target matching/factor having a different number of gadget lifts, or a gadget violating simplicity or the size bound.
claims.next_gate: No further work unless a nontrivial weighted or otherwise richer extension with a separately proved polynomial-bit reduction is identified.

claims.exact_statement: The approximate-sampling/fixed-k/f-factor branch does not provide an independent novelty claim beyond the pinned manuscript and established self-reducibility; the sampler is not exact uniform and arbitrary weighted inputs are outside the stated interface.
assumptions: Pinned manuscript contents and cited primary prior art accurately represented
